title: Project taxonomy, typed custom fields and safe activation
summary: Workflow/stage/transition/binding/migration and review-policy setup are canonical in workflows; this area retains taxonomy, defaults, custom-field lifecycle and activation guards. Existing test references do not certify execution or per-case coverage.

cases.title: Explain filtered default board
preconditions: The actor has the stated role in a current project; mutations use its latest configuration revision unless a conflict case states otherwise.
steps: Review readiness when the default board has saved filters.
expected: A default_filters problem requires complete project coverage.
notes: Defensive historical-data acceptance: ordinary current API writes cannot produce this state because the named PostgreSQL CHECK rejects it. A guarded disposable-database fixture captures that exact validated CHECK, changes only its owned retained row while dropping/restoring the identical CHECK NOT VALID in one transaction, proves later writes remain protected, and finally repairs the row and validates the CHECK. Actual Go readiness responses and rendered UI warnings are then tested; no normal-user corruption or production schema change is claimed.

cases.title: Explain canonical-reference gap
preconditions: The actor has the stated role in a current project; mutations use its latest configuration revision unless a conflict case states otherwise.
steps: Review readiness before canonical issue references are complete.
expected: A canonical_references problem is returned.
notes: Defensive historical-data acceptance: ordinary current API writes cannot produce this state because the named PostgreSQL CHECK rejects it. A guarded disposable-database fixture captures that exact validated CHECK, changes only its owned retained row while dropping/restoring the identical CHECK NOT VALID in one transaction, proves later writes remain protected, and finally repairs the row and validates the CHECK. Actual Go readiness responses and rendered UI warnings are then tested; no normal-user corruption or production schema change is claimed.

The retained null-reference fixture also captures and restores the exact enabled issues_canonical_shape trigger within the same locked transaction. Both its new-write rejection and the restored CHECK are proved before commit; finally the owned row is repaired and the identical CHECK validated.
